title: Anticoagulation Reversal Reference
sources: Bekka et al. Br J Clin Pharmacol 2025

changelog.change: Removed andexanet alfa as primary US recommendation following Dec 22 2025 US market withdrawal; 4F-PCC now primary for US practice.

summary: Reversal agents by anticoagulant class. This record is the reference implementation of the Content Update Architecture — the andexanet correction was a JSON edit + version bump, not an App Store resubmission.

body.text: Andexanet alfa was voluntarily withdrawn from the US market on 2026-12-22 (thromboembolic safety concerns) — corrected here as content_version 3. It remains available in the EU/Canada; a non-US build should branch on region.

items: 4-factor PCC, dosed by INR and weight, for life-threatening bleeding or urgent surgery
Vitamin K 10 mg IV over 30 minutes — the single correct dose/route for emergent reversal (co-administer with PCC; PCC effect is transient)
Idarucizumab 5 g IV, given as two 2.5 g infusions
Consider hemodialysis (dabigatran is dialyzable) if idarucizumab unavailable
US practice: 4-factor PCC 50 units/kg (or per institutional protocol) — current practical default
Andexanet alfa: no longer available in the US as of 2026-12-22; still an option in the EU/Canada
Activated charcoal if last dose within 2-4 hours

rows: Vitamin K 10 mg IV over 30 min
